item.title: Development of a Prototype Superconducting Radio-Frequency Multicell Cavity for Compact, Conduction-Cooled Accelerators
item.description: arXiv:2610.28870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jefferson Lab and General Atomics are jointly advancing compact, high-power irradiation systems capable of delivering electron-beam powers in the hundreds of kilowatts based on superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) technology. A critical step toward deploying SRF accelerators in industrial environments is replacing traditional liquid-helium cryogenic systems with conduction-cooled cryomodules powered by commercial cryocoolers. This paper reports recent progress in the design, fabrication, and testing of a prototype three-cell SRF cavity developed at Jefferson Lab and evaluated in a dedicated horizontal test cryostat at General Atomics. Peak surface magnetic fields up to 18.4\,mT, corresponding to accelerating gradients of approximately 4.3\,MV/m, were achieved in one of the cells. The results provide key insights into cavity preparation, thin-film coating, mechanical robustness, and cryogenic integration, offering guidance for the continued maturation of compact, conduction-cooled SRF accelerators for industrial irradiation applications.

item.title: Oscillation modes, Decoherence, Beam Transfer Functions, and Instabilities for a Beam Subjected to Space-Charge Forces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the oscillation modes of a bunch subject to the space-charge force, we discuss the decoherence of the dipole oscillation, the beam transfer function, and the beam instability. The longitudinal phase space is discretized into \(n_l\times n_J\) grids in the azimuthal and radial directions, respectively. The transverse dipole moment in the longitudinal phase space is represented by a vector of length \(n_l n_J\), and the transformation given by the Vlasov equation is represented by a matrix transformation of size \(n_l n_J\times n_l n_J\). Solving the eigenvalue problem of this matrix gives the \(n_l n_J\) eigen-oscillation modes of the bunch. Using the resulting eigenvectors within a standard linear-algebraic treatment, we analyze these three phenomena. The analysis was performed for the Rapid Cycling Synchrotron (RCS) of the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) using \(n_l=41\) and \(n_J=40\), and it visualizes the features related to the continuous distribution of the tune, Landau damping, and isolated modes separated from the continuous tune region.
item.dc:creator: Kazuhito Ohmi, Liangsheng Huang, Hanyang Liu, Li Rao, Renjun Yang, Sheng Wang, Mingyang Huang

item.title: Evaluation of Transverse Incoherent Tune Shifts in the Electron-Ion Collider
item.description: arXiv:2610.29951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) peak luminosity goal of 10 to the power of 34 per square centimeter per second requires high average currents, flat beams, non-circular vacuum chambers, and large transverse orbit offsets in the Hadron Storage Ring (HSR) and Electron Storage Ring (ESR). These conditions can generate collective effects and incoherent tune spreads that drive particles across low-order betatron resonances, causing emittance growth, halo formation, and reduced beam lifetime. We quantitatively evaluate incoherent transverse betatron tune shifts from beam-beam interactions, direct space charge, and beam-environment interactions associated with image forces and vacuum chamber geometry. Xsuite and PyHEADTAIL simulations validate the analytical calculations for beam-beam and direct space-charge effects, respectively. For indirect space-charge effects, we review and compare several analytical formalisms and apply the Laslett image-charge formulation to rectangular vacuum chambers with off-axis beams. The analysis accounts for transverse orbit offsets of up to 20 mm in the HSR and 10 mm in the ESR. The results establish baseline parameters and provide quantitative guidance for EIC design, optimization, and operation. The comparison of indirect space-charge formalisms also offers an accessible reference and methodology for studies of high-intensity beam dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Xiaofeng Gu, Alexei Blednykh
